mechanics.claim: Aphelios has 5 weapons and is only ever equipped with 2 (main and off-hand); he starts with Calibrum main / Severum off-hand, and Gravitum, Infernum, Crescendum queued in reserve in that order.
mechanics.quote: '''Aphelios''' begins the game with {{ai|Calibrum|Aphelios}} as his {{as|main weapon}} and {{ai|Severum|Aphelios}} in his {{as|off-hand}}, with {{ai|Gravitum|Aphelios}}, {{ai|Infernum|Aphelios}}, and {{ai|Crescendum|Aphelios}} queued in reserve.

mechanics.claim: Moonlight is spent on every basic attack and on every Q cast, but abilities that make Aphelios auto-attack as part of their effect (Onslaught, Duskwave's follow-up, Sentry) do not spend additional Moonlight for those attacks.
mechanics.quote: Any of his abilities that automatically cause him to attack during their effect will not consume additional ''Moonlight''.

mechanics.claim: When the main weapon's Moonlight hits zero it goes to the back of the reserve queue and Alune assembles the next weapon; Aphelios cannot toggle Phase during that assembly.
mechanics.quote: '''Aphelios''' cannot cast ''{{ai|Phase|Aphelios}}'' during the assembly.

mechanics.claim: Calibrum's empowered snipe is fired by whichever weapon is currently the main weapon if Calibrum itself is off-hand (the off-hand weapon fires it only when Calibrum is main).
mechanics.quote: If '''Calibrum''' is the current {{as|off-hand}} weapon, the {{as|main weapon}} is used for the attack instead.

mechanics.claim: The empowered snipe consumes the mark(s) on whatever targets currently carry one; against a single target only one mark can be outstanding (it is a duration debuff, not a stacking counter), so at most one 15 (+15% bonus AD) instance is dealt per snipe in a single-target fight.
mechanics.quote: The empowered attack will consume the marks from all targets, dealing {{as|15|physical damage}} {{as|(+ 15% '''bonus''' AD)}} {{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}} to the main target for each mark consumed.

mechanics.claim: Gravitum's basic attack applies a slow (30% decaying to 15% after 0.7s over 2.5s total) but no bonus damage; the slow itself is a pure utility effect the damage fight does not score, though its presence on the target is what Binding Eclipse (Q) requires to be castable.
mechanics.quote: Basic attacks with '''Gravitum''' {{tip|slow}} enemies by 30% for {{fd|2.5}} seconds, decaying to 15% after {{fd|0.7}} seconds.

mechanics.claim: Infernum's fire bolt splits into a cone of secondary bolts behind the primary target; against a single stationary dummy with no other enemies, there is nothing behind the target for these bolts to hit, so this component of Infernum's attack never deals damage in this fight.
mechanics.quote: shoot a fire bolt that upon arrival splits into a cone of 4 lesser bolts behind the target, dealing damage to enemies they pass through

mechanics.claim: Crescendum's basic attack throws the blade and Aphelios cannot attack again until it returns to him (a self-inflicted attack lock whose length depends on travel distance to and from the target).
mechanics.quote: He is unable to declare basic attacks until he retrieves '''Crescendum''', but the attack timer is reset {{tt|once caught|This does not persist when swapping weapons.}}.

mechanics.claim: While holding Chakrams, Crescendum's own attack windup is reduced (further reduced again on a crit), independent of the per-Chakram bonus damage.
mechanics.quote: have a lower {{tip|attack windup|windup}} of {{ap|0.159999996423721/1.5*100|round=2}}%, further decreased to {{ap|0.100000001490116/1.5*100|round=2}}% when {{tip|critically strike|critically striking}}

mechanics.claim: Weapon Master's three statistics are ranked with the Q, W and E level-up keys (attack damage, attack speed, lethality), and a statistic can reach rank 1 to 6 no earlier than levels 1, 2, 3, 5, 7 and 9. With 18 skill points and three statistics of 6 ranks, everything is maxed at level 18; at level 16 the statistic ranked last has 4 of its 6 ranks.
mechanics.quote: the earliest level that an individual statistic can attain rank 6 is level 9, by assigning points at levels {{ap|1|2|3|5|7|9}}

mechanics.claim: When the main weapon runs out of Moonlight the next weapon is assembled over 1 second, with its Q held on cooldown for 1.5 seconds from the start of the assembly; the off-hand weapon is not touched. A spent weapon re-enters the queue with 50 Moonlight.
mechanics.quote: Once his {{as|main weapon's}} ''Moonlight'' is exhausted, it is moved to the end of the reserve queue; '''Alune''' then assembles his next available weapon from the reserve over 1 second, placing its {{cci|Q.png|champion ability|primary ability}} on a {{fd|1.5}}-second {{sti|cooldown}} from the start of the assembly.

mechanics.claim: A mark-consuming attack is a basic attack in the attack cycle (since V10.4 it no longer resets the attack timer) that applies on-hit effects once and stacks Energized, but triggers no other on-attack effect.
mechanics.quote: Triggered ''Marks'' apply on-hit effects, stack {{nie|Energized}} and trigger {{ii|Runaan's Hurricane}}, but no other [[on-attack effects]].

mechanics.claim: Chakrams are lost when Crescendum runs out of Moonlight, and their 5 s timer restarts whenever a new one is caught or a champion is attacked with Crescendum, so they last as long as Crescendum keeps attacking.
mechanics.quote: which last for 5 seconds or until '''Crescendum''' is depleted of ''Moonlight''. ''Chakram'' duration is refreshed when '''Aphelios''' catches a new one or attacks a {{tip|champion}} with '''Crescendum'''.

mechanics.claim: The attack timer is reset when Crescendum is caught, so its cadence is the flight itself: the windup, the way out, the 0.2 s at the target and the way back. At range and at high attack speed that is slower than an ordinary attack.
mechanics.quote: Due to the return time, at high attack speeds '''Crescendum''' will increase '''Aphelios' '''effective time to cast attacks, even when right next to his target.

mechanics.claim: The five weapon Q actives do not share a cooldown with each other.
mechanics.quote: The individual actives do not share a cooldown.

mechanics.claim: Onslaught's cooldown starts only after the 1.75s automatic-attack effect ends, not at the moment of casting.

mechanics.claim: Onslaught's attacks are affected by critical strike modifiers and apply on-hit effects (at reduced effectiveness, see values); Aphelios cannot cast Phase or Moonlight Vigil during Onslaught but can still move.
mechanics.quote: '''''Aphelios''' cannot cast {{ai|Phase|Aphelios}} nor {{ai|Moonlight Vigil|Aphelios}} during Onslaught, but he is still able to move.''

mechanics.claim: Onslaught fires its first automatic attack with Aphelios's off-hand weapon, then alternates.
mechanics.quote: ''Onslaught'' begins firing with '''Aphelios'''' {{as|off-hand}} weapon.

mechanics.claim: Each Onslaught attack counts as a separate cast instance for cast-triggered item/rune effects (e.g. Electrocute, Eclipse).
mechanics.quote: Each attack of ''Onslaught'' counts as a separate {{tip|cast instance}} for effects such as {{ri|Electrocute}} and {{iis|Eclipse}} {{nie|Ever Rising Moon}}.

mechanics.claim: Binding Eclipse can only be cast on an enemy currently affected by Gravitum's slow, or on an in-flight Gravitum projectile (which it then empowers to apply the effect on arrival); it cannot simply be cast on cooldown like the other weapons' Qs.
mechanics.quote: An enemy affected by Gravitum, or an in-flight Gravitum projectile, is required to cast this ability.

mechanics.claim: Aphelios is locked out of declaring (Crescendum-style) attacks until Duskwave's volley of attacks has resolved, and the volley's damage is affected by critical strike modifiers.
mechanics.quote: '''Aphelios''' is locked out of declaring attacks until the volley of attacks has resolved.

mechanics.claim: The sentry deployed by Sentry gains a copy of Aphelios's current off-hand weapon and benefits from his attack speed and critical strike chance at 100% effectiveness; it can also critically strike.

mechanics.claim: The dummy in this fight never attacks, so the sentry is never destroyed by return fire; its practical lifetime in the fight is bounded only by its own arm/active-duration timers.
mechanics.quote: Sentries have {{as|6 health}} and take 3 damage per {{tip|ranged}} basic attack and 4 damage per hit by abilities.

mechanics.claim: Onslaught's attack count is 6 x (1 + 0.33334 x bonus attack speed) in Riot's file: the coefficient is a hair over one third, so 50% and 100% bonus attack speed land just above 7 and 8 and the count reads as rounded down.
mechanics.quote: automatically performing up to 6 {{as|(+ 2 per 100% '''bonus''' attack speed)|attack speed}} attacks over the duration

mechanics.claim: Onslaught's attacks apply on-hit effects at 25% damage (Kraken Slayer's proc included, per the V11.2 and V11.6 patch history) and stack Energized, but trigger no other on-attack effect; they never consume a Calibrum mark.
mechanics.quote: ''Onslaught's'' attacks stack {{tip|Energized}}, but do not apply any other {{tip|on-attack}} effects.

mechanics.claim: During Onslaught an attack command only moves Aphelios, so no basic attack is made until it ends.

mechanics.claim: Duskwave's volley applies on-hit effects but no on-attack effects (the two statements are about different things, not a contradiction), and no attack can be declared until the volley has gone out, which therefore comes after the 0.4 s cast time: 0.25 s after it.
mechanics.quote: '''Aphelios''' is locked out of declaring attacks until the volley of attacks has resolved.

mechanics.claim: The sentry attacks at 0.64 base attack speed with a 0.64 attack speed ratio on Aphelios's bonus attack speed (the Pets infobox of the wiki's champion page, and V13.13's 'Turret attack speed reduced to 0.64 from 0.8'; the ability templates archived here do not repeat it). Its attacks are spell damage and apply no on-hit effects.

primitives.note: The core of the kit: 5 weapons, 2 equipped at once (main/off-hand), each with its own Moonlight ammo (50/weapon, 1 per attack, 10 per Q cast), auto-swapping on empty; Phase (W) manually swaps, E only displays the queue.
Each weapon is effectively a separate form: a distinct basic-attack effect (P) and a distinct Q active, swapped in and out as main/off-hand change.
Moonshot, Binding Eclipse, Duskwave's initial cone hit and Moonlight Vigil's initial smite all deal damage on a fixed cast time (or short travel delay), on cooldown.
Duskwave (cone, then a 0.25s-delayed off-hand volley) and Moonlight Vigil (smite, then 0.3s-delayed sky-attacks) each resolve as two separately timed damage instances from one cast.
Calibrum's mark arms the next basic attack for bonus damage; Moonlight Vigil's sky-attacks are a similar armed/delayed attack against each locked-on target.
Infernum's total-attack multiplier (110% AD) and Crescendum's per-Chakram bonus both ride on ordinary basic attacks.
Crescendum's own attack timer is reset once the thrown blade is caught (locks out attacking until then).
Crescendum's held Chakrams: cap 20, 5s expiry refreshed by catching/attacking, diminishing bonus AD per stack (15% down to a 5% floor).
Calibrum's mark is a target-side flag (applied by Calibrum abilities/R) later consumed by the empowered snipe.
Moonlight ammo and mana genuinely bound how many attacks/casts happen in a 15s fight.
Infernum's crit sprays 6 missiles instead of 4; Onslaught/Duskwave's volley/Sentry/R's sky-attacks all crit (Sentry at 100% AS/crit-chance effectiveness); R adds its own extra crit-damage modifier.
Onslaught's attack count scales with bonus attack speed; Crescendum's attack windup is reduced (further on crit); Sentry benefits from Aphelios's attack speed.
Sentry deploys a lunar sentry that autonomously attacks with a copy of the off-hand weapon.

Crescendum's throw-and-return travel time depends on distance to the target; Infernum's secondary/cone bolts require other enemies behind the target, which a single dummy fight does not have; Sentry's activation depends on placement.
Weapon Master: Q unlocks at champion level 2, R at 6 and auto-upgrades at 11 and 16.

needsBespoke.why: A generic rank/level-scaled ability model cannot express: (1) the weapon state machine itself -- which of 5 weapons is main vs off-hand vs reserve, gating which P attack-effect and which Q are active, and changing over the fight as ammo depletes or Phase is toggled; (2) several abilities' damage depends on whichever OTHER weapon is currently off-hand/main at the moment they resolve (Calibrum's empowered snipe always fires with the off-hand weapon; Onslaught/Duskwave/Sentry's follow-ups use the off-hand weapon; R's bonus effect depends on the main weapon at cast time), i.e. cross-weapon dependencies, not a single ability's own rank; (3) Crescendum's per-Chakram bonus is a diminishing, capped, expiring stack curve (15% down to a 5% floor per stack, 20-stack cap, 5s refreshed expiry), not a linear coefficient; (4) Crescendum's attack cadence depends on projectile travel time to and from the target (geometry), not a fixed attack windup; (5) Binding Eclipse is only castable once a precondition (a live Gravitum slow or in-flight projectile) is met, not simply off cooldown.

unsettled.question: Which two weapons, with how much Moonlight, does a level 16 fight start from? A fight of 8 to 15 seconds never cycles through the arsenal, so the loadout it starts with decides which two Qs and which attack effects it has.
options: The kit's own starting state: Calibrum as main weapon, Severum in the off-hand, Gravitum, Infernum and Crescendum queued, 50 Moonlight each.
Another of the 10 weapon pairs (the default order passes through Severum + Gravitum, Gravitum + Infernum, Infernum + Crescendum and Crescendum + Calibrum as the game goes on).
quotes: begins the game with {{ai|Calibrum|Aphelios}} as his {{as|main weapon}} and {{ai|Severum|Aphelios}} in his {{as|off-hand}}

unsettled.question: What distance does a Crescendum attack (and a spectral Chakram) fly? The way out, the 0.2 s at the target and the way back are the whole attack interval, and neither source states a fight distance.
options: Aphelios's own attack range (550): the one distance the engine already assumes for a target, and the slow reading at high attack speed.
Point-blank, where the round trip is short and Crescendum attacks far faster than attack speed allows any other weapon.
quotes: which lingers for {{fd|0.2}} seconds before homing back to '''Aphelios'''
He is unable to declare basic attacks until he retrieves '''Crescendum'''

unsettled.question: Can Aphelios attack during the 1 second in which the next weapon is assembled? The wiki names only Phase as unavailable.
options: No: he has no main weapon until the assembly ends, so no attack and no cast starts inside it (what guides describe: a 1 second animation with no attacks or abilities).
Yes: only Phase and the new weapon's Q are locked.

unsettled.question: Do off-hand attacks made by abilities carry the weapon's own attack bonus: Infernum's 110% AD on an Onslaught or Sentry hit, Crescendum's Chakram bonus on a spectral Chakram?
options: No: an ability's attack deals the ability's stated damage; only a basic attack (a mark-consuming one included) deals the firing weapon's attack damage.
Yes: every attack a weapon makes carries its bonus.
quotes: The fire bolt deals {{as|110% AD}} {{as|physical damage}} to the primary target.
Attacks with '''Crescendum''' are empowered to deal

unsettled.question: Can a single target carry more than one Calibrum mark?
options: No: a mark is a debuff on the target, so a single target gives one mark per consuming attack however often it is marked again.
Yes: marks accumulate on one target.
quotes: Enemies damaged by '''Calibrum''' through an ability are marked for {{fd|4.5}} seconds
The empowered attack will consume the marks from all targets

proposal: Start from the kit's own loadout: Calibrum main, Severum off-hand, Gravitum, Infernum and Crescendum queued, 50 Moonlight each.
Attack first, then weave every cast into the gap after an attack lands: a cast that ends before the next attack would start costs no attack at all.

Moonlight Vigil goes out after the first attack with whichever held weapon gives it the most damage (Crescendum's 6 Chakrams, then Infernum's bonus blast, then Calibrum's empowered mark), swapping with Phase first when that weapon is in the off-hand.

Each weapon's Q is cast when that weapon is main and the Q is up: Sentry, Duskwave, Moonshot (once the previous mark is consumed), Binding Eclipse (once a Gravitum hit has slowed the target), and Onslaught when its shots are worth more than the attacks its 1.75 s replaces.

Phase to the off-hand when its Q is up and the main weapon has nothing to cast, and otherwise keep the weapon whose attacks deal more as the main weapon (Infernum's 110% AD, Crescendum with Chakrams).
Mana is never the limit inside a fight of this length.
